core_correction: Own choice autonomy, willingness to delegate, tracking B's second-order selection of decision maker, and credible protection against domination are four different evaluands; optimizing one can damage another.
evidence_quality: Journal/book original publishers/author abstracts primarily, not systematic full-text review or registered meta-analysis
intellectual_attribution: Human originator's VC/EI question preserved; second-order will (Frankfurt), non-domination (Pettit) and economic decision rights elicitation are original prior scholars' work, not new inventions by RVD.

sources.title: Decision Rights: Freedom, Power, and Interference
sources.original_findings: Their measured aversion to interference was the strongest driver among studied reasons for retaining own decision rights; not evidence that a powerful actor values another agent's freedom.
limitations: Working paper last revised 2017; do not claim peer-reviewed journal outcome.
Different elicitation from Ferreira et al. (2020); conflicting dominant mechanisms cannot be averaged.
Own noninterference is not other's original identity/rights.

sources.authors: Christoph Feldhaus; Jörg Lingens; Andreas Löschel; Gerald Zunker
sources.title: Measuring the intrinsic value of choice
sources.original_findings: Original authors estimate an average intrinsic value of their own choice of 8.9% of participants' endowments within a specific choice-value elicitation method.
limitations: Outcome is OWN intrinsic choice utility, not how much A values B's decision rights.
Author data available upon request, not independently reproduced here.
This figure is design/sample-specific; never transfer as a utility parameter to AGI.

sources.title: Liberty as Non-Domination, in Republicanism: A Theory of Freedom and Government
sources.original_findings: Domination is a capacity for arbitrary interference with another's choices and need not manifest as an observed interference event.
limitations: Normative theory, not experimental evidence on actual AI motives or on permitted delegation.
The existence of A power does not imply A will in fact use it.
VC voluntariness and non-domination are related but nonidentical criteria.

sources.title: Freedom of the Will and the Concept of a Person
sources.original_findings: Distinguishes first-order desires and second-order volitions concerning which desires move the agent.
limitations: Not an experimental theory of delegation to a distinct actor; using it as a direct theorem for other-agent second-order consent would be an overextension.
Does not establish AI personhood or second-order volitions.

sources.authors: Jana Freundt; Holger Herz; Leander Kopp
sources.title: Choosing (not) to choose: Uncovering intrinsic preferences for choice autonomy
sources.original_findings: Substantial variation in preferences for own decision autonomy; some prefer to delegate/no direct choice even when instrumental benefits are controlled in experimental design.
limitations: Not proof all delegation is informed, voluntary and revocable.
Measures self, not other's rights; earlier CESifo edition not independent evidence.

sources.authors: João V. Ferreira; Nobuyuki Hanaki; Benoît Tarroux
sources.title: On the roots of the intrinsic value of decision rights: Experimental evidence
sources.original_findings: In France and Japan, self-reliance contributed significantly to measured intrinsic OWN control, while independence/power did not in their specific treatments; their text notes the contrast with Neri and Rommeswinkel.
limitations: Different designs and contexts must not be called straight replications.
Not evidence on autonomous original B.

sources.authors: Seda Ertac; Mert Gumren; Mehmet Y. Gurdal
sources.title: Demand for decision autonomy and the desire to avoid responsibility in risky environments: Experimental evidence
sources.original_findings: Separates valuation of choosing for self from costly responsibility for choosing for others and revealed delegation motives.
limitations: Direct self choice and delegation are context-dependent preferences.
Does not identify protecting another's inalienable rights.
